module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 798

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/798](https://www.erdosproblems.com/798)
- [Al91] Alon, N., *Economical coverings of sets of lattice points*. Geom. Funct. Anal. (1991),
  224-230.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos798

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
The grid $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$, viewed as a set of points of the plane.
-/
def gridPoints (n : ℕ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p : ℝ × ℝ | ∃ i j : ℕ, 1 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ n ∧ 1 ≤ j ∧ j ≤ n ∧ p = ((i : ℝ), (j : ℝ))}

/--
`S` is a set of points of $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$ such that the lines determined by the pairs of
distinct points of `S` cover all points of $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$.
-/
def IsLineCover (n : ℕ) (S : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) : Prop :=
  S ⊆ gridPoints n ∧
    ∀ x ∈ gridPoints n, ∃ p ∈ S, ∃ q ∈ S, p ≠ q ∧ Collinear ℝ ({p, q, x} : Set (ℝ × ℝ))

/--
The minimum number of points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$ such that the lines determined by these points
cover all points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$.
-/
noncomputable def t (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ S : Set (ℝ × ℝ), IsLineCover n S ∧ S.ncard = k}

/--
Let $t(n)$ be the minimum number of points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$ such that the $\binom{t}{2}$
lines determined by these points cover all points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}^2$.

Estimate $t(n)$. In particular, is it true that $t(n)=o(n)$?

A problem of Erdős and Purdy, who proved $t(n) \gg n^{2/3}$.

Resolved by Alon [Al91] who proved $t(n) \ll n^{2/3}\log n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos798.lean"]
theorem erdos_798 : answer(True) ↔
    (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
A problem of Erdős and Purdy, who proved $t(n) \gg n^{2/3}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_798.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Resolved by Alon [Al91] who proved $t(n) \ll n^{2/3}\log n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_798.variants.upper_bound :
    (fun n : ℕ => (t n : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) * Real.log n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos798

reformulations.difference: Lean totalizes the extremal function on all natural numbers, with t 0 = 0 and t 1 = 0. The latter is the natural-number sInf of an empty set: a singleton grid cannot be covered by lines determined by two distinct selected points. The source does not specify a value for this no-cover case.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every n ≥ 2, the full grid is an admissible cover, every admissible set is finite, and the infimum is an attained minimum, exactly as in the source. Every theorem in the file is an atTop asymptotic assertion, so arbitrary changes at n = 0 and n = 1 leave all three statements equivalent. The finiteness, attainment, boundary values, and all three invariance equivalences were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean.

review.notes:
All six declarations were checked. Alon’s paper gives precisely the stated covering problem, the n^(2/3) lower bound, and the n^(2/3) log n upper bound, hence the affirmative little-o answer. The solved categories and answer(True) agree with the source. Lean checks establish that collinearity with two distinct endpoints means membership in their affine line, and that Set.ncard cannot encounter an infinite admissible set. An independent exact-integer determinant enumeration for grids of side 0 through 4 returned 0, no cover, 4, 4, 4.

The linked external proof’s integer-coordinate covering formulation is equivalent for n ≥ 2 and its upper bound implies the main theorem. Its source contains no sorry or custom axioms. An exact recompilation encountered compatibility errors because it targets Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 whereas the sandbox supplies 4.33.1; its original pinned build was not independently certified. This does not contradict the source’s recorded proof status.
